subject: Reasoning
topic: Course of Action and Critical Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statement: The number of road accidents in the city has increased by 40% in the past year.
Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?
I. The government should impose a complete ban on all vehicles.
II. Traffic police should increase patrolling and enforce traffic rules more strictly.

options.option_text: Only I follows (banning all vehicles is an extreme and impractical measure)
Only II follows (correct: stricter enforcement is a direct, practical response to rising accidents ✓)
Both I and II follow (I is too extreme)
Neither I nor II follows (II is clearly an appropriate measure)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Course of Action rule: the action must be practical, proportional, and directly address the problem. II (increase patrolling and enforce traffic rules) is a direct, feasible response to rising accidents. I (ban all vehicles) is disproportionate and not practical. Only II follows.

questions.stem:
Statement: A large number of students in a school are failing in mathematics.
Course of action:
I. The school should immediately expel all failing students.
II. The school should arrange for extra coaching and remedial classes in mathematics.

options.option_text: Only I follows (expelling students doesn't solve the learning problem)
Only II follows (correct: remedial classes address the root cause — lack of understanding — directly and constructively ✓)
Both I and II follow (I is punitive, not constructive)
Neither follows (II is clearly appropriate)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Expelling students (I) punishes them and doesn't improve their mathematical understanding. Remedial classes (II) directly address the gap in learning. A good course of action solves the problem, not just eliminates the symptom. Only II follows.

questions.stem:
Statement: The water supply in the city has become contaminated due to sewage leakage.
Courses of action:
I. The authorities should repair the sewage pipeline immediately.
II. Citizens should be advised to boil water before drinking until repairs are done.

options.option_text: Only I follows (I alone is necessary but II provides immediate protection during repair time)
Only II follows (II is a stopgap — root cause still needs fixing)
Both I and II follow (correct: I fixes the root cause; II provides immediate interim protection — both are practical and proportionate ✓)
Neither follows (both are clearly necessary responses)

questions.explanation: C is correct. Both actions are necessary and complementary: I fixes the root cause (sewage leakage). II provides immediate public health protection while repairs take time. When a problem has both a root-cause fix and an interim safety measure, both courses of action are valid.

questions.stem:
Statement: A famous restaurant has been found to be serving adulterated food.
Courses of action:
I. The restaurant should be immediately shut down pending investigation.
II. The owner should be given a warning letter and allowed to continue operations.

options.option_text: Only I follows (correct: food adulteration is a serious public health hazard; immediate closure protects consumers; a warning letter (II) is insufficient given the severity ✓)
Only II follows (a warning letter is too lenient for food adulteration)
Both I and II follow (they contradict each other — can't close AND continue operations)
Neither follows (I is clearly appropriate)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Adulterated food is a serious public health risk. Immediate closure (I) is a necessary protective measure — it prevents further harm while an investigation occurs. A warning letter (II) is insufficient; it allows continued risk. The two actions also contradict each other. Only I follows.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Majority of the employees in the company feel that the new performance appraisal system is unfair.'
Which conclusion logically follows?
I. The company should immediately abandon the new system.
II. The management should review the appraisal criteria and discuss concerns with employees.

options.option_text: Only I follows (abandoning immediately is rash — there may be valid elements in the system)
Only II follows (correct: when employees feel a system is unfair, review and dialogue is the appropriate measured response ✓)
Both I and II follow (I is too extreme without investigation first)
Neither follows (II is clearly the correct course)

questions.explanation: B is correct. The fact that employees 'feel' the system is unfair doesn't mean it actually is — review and dialogue (II) is the proportionate response. Immediate abandonment (I) is reactive and doesn't validate or understand the concern first. Good course-of-action responses are measured and address root concerns constructively.

questions.stem:
Statement: A sudden outbreak of dengue fever has been reported in a locality.
Courses of action:
I. People should be educated about eliminating mosquito breeding sites.
II. Fogging and spraying operations should be carried out in the affected area.
III. A 24-hour medical helpline should be established for the affected locality.

options.option_text: Only I and II follow (III is also appropriate during a health emergency)
Only II and III follow (I — public education — is also necessary for prevention)
All I, II, and III follow (correct: I=prevention, II=elimination of mosquitoes, III=medical support — all are practical and complementary ✓)
Only I follows (prevention alone is insufficient for an active outbreak)

questions.explanation: C is correct. A dengue outbreak requires a multi-pronged response: I (public education) prevents new breeding sites; II (fogging) eliminates current mosquitoes; III (helpline) provides medical access for those already affected. All three are practical, proportionate, and complementary. All three follow.

questions.stem:
Statement: The government has decided to increase taxes on luxury goods.
Assumptions:
I. People who buy luxury goods can afford to pay higher taxes.
II. Increased taxes will discourage the purchase of luxury goods.

options.option_text: Only assumption I is implicit (correct: taxing luxury goods assumes the buyers can afford it — otherwise the policy would be counterproductive. Assumption II may or may not be the government's intent ✓)
Only assumption II is implicit (may be one motive, but I is more fundamental — the tax must be payable)
Both I and II are implicit (II is a possible intent but not a necessary assumption; I is a necessary precondition for the policy)
Neither I nor II is implicit (I is clearly a fundamental assumption of any luxury tax)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Assumption I ('buyers can afford higher taxes') is implicit because the entire policy of taxing luxury goods presupposes that those who buy such items are in a financial position to pay more. This is a necessary assumption — without it, the policy is meaningless. Assumption II describes a possible outcome (price elasticity) but is not necessarily assumed by the government.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'People who exercise regularly are less likely to develop chronic diseases.'
Which of the following conclusions is valid?
I. All people who develop chronic diseases do not exercise.
II. Regular exercise reduces the risk of developing chronic diseases.

options.option_text: Only I follows (the statement says 'less likely' — not 'impossible'; I overstates this)
Only II follows (correct: 'less likely' directly translates to 'reduced risk'; II accurately reflects the statement ✓)
Both I and II follow (I is too absolute — 'less likely' ≠ 'all non-exercisers get disease')
Neither follows (II logically follows directly from the statement)

questions.explanation: B is correct. The statement says exercise makes people 'less likely' to develop chronic disease. Conclusion II ('reduces risk') is a faithful restatement. Conclusion I ('all people who develop chronic diseases don't exercise') is too absolute — people who exercise can still develop chronic diseases; the statement says probability is reduced, not eliminated. Only II follows.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Studies show that children who read for at least 30 minutes daily perform significantly better academically.'
Conclusions:
I. All good students read for at least 30 minutes daily.
II. Encouraging daily reading habits may improve children's academic performance.

options.option_text: Only I follows (I is too absolute — 'significantly better' doesn't mean ALL good students read)
Only II follows (correct: II is a measured, practical conclusion consistent with the evidence cited ✓)
Both I and II follow (I makes an absolute claim not supported by the statement)
Neither follows (II directly follows from the study cited)

questions.explanation: B is correct. The statement establishes a correlation: reading ≥30 min/day correlates with better academic performance. Conclusion II ('may improve performance') is a careful, evidence-based suggestion. Conclusion I ('ALL good students read') is an absolute claim not supported — correlation doesn't imply universality or reverse causation. Only II follows.

questions.stem:
Statement: The crime rate in city X has dropped by 30% after the introduction of CCTV cameras.
Course of action:
I. CCTV cameras should be installed in other cities as well to reduce crime.
II. All existing cameras should be removed after confirming the drop in crime.

options.option_text: Only I follows (correct: the evidence shows cameras reduce crime — extending this to other cities is a logical course of action; removing them (II) would reverse progress ✓)
Only II follows (removing cameras after success would reverse the crime reduction)
Both I and II follow (II is counterproductive — they contradict each other)
Neither follows (I clearly follows from the evidence)

questions.explanation: A is correct. The data shows CCTV cameras reduced crime by 30%. Extending this proven measure to other cities (I) is a logical scale-up response. Removing the cameras (II) would likely reverse the drop — it is illogical given the evidence. Only I follows.
